title: Replicating CoT Monitoring with Adversarially Fine-Tuned Agent: Does the Advantage Persist?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Directly tests a critical assumption underlying CoT monitoring: that models do not optimize to evade it. If the monitoring advantage collapses under adversarial fine-tuning, this invalidates a major proposed control measure. Every link in the chain is explicit and high-stakes.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires RL fine-tuning of a model with a custom reward signal that rewards evasion of a CoT monitor. Setting up the RL loop (PPO or similar), defining the reward correctly, and running adversarial fine-tuning is well beyond beginner ML scope even with mentor support. Medium compute may be tight for RL training.

narrow_scope.reasoning: The RL fine-tuning loop alone could consume the entire 30-hour budget. Debugging reward functions, iterating on hyperparameters, and running evaluation adds significant time. Not feasible for beginners in 30 hours.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
